name: QTS Blakely Campus
heading: 3. QTS Blakely Campus — 1,400 MW Potential Gross Capacity
brief: The proposed QTS campus in Blakely , Early County, is a rare example of a developer publishing a direct, full-scale energy figure while acknowledging how early the project remains. QTS’s own site states 1,400 MW of potential gross capacity for the concept. Gross infrastructure capacity can include mechanical systems and other overhead outside the servers themselves. It is not a contracted 1.4 GW IT workload, an approved delivery schedule or an operating load.

name: Project Bunkhouse, Bartow County
heading: 2. Project Bunkhouse, Bartow County — 1,830 MW Early Site-Plan Demand
brief: The approximately 877-acre Project Bunkhouse site sits near Taff Road and Georgia Power’s Plant Bowen , northwest of Atlanta. An April 2025 Atlanta Journal-Constitution review of early plans reported 1,830 MW of possible power demand and three on-site substations. The initial state Development of Regional Impact filing, #4433 , described a campus approaching 8.7 million square feet and a possible investment of $19 billion at full buildout.

name: OpenAI Project Camellia, Effingham County
heading: 1. OpenAI Project Camellia, Effingham County — 3,200 MW Utility Agreement
brief: OpenAI’s Project Camellia , planned for the Savannah Gateway Industrial Hub in Effingham County, leads this ranking with an explicitly announced 3.2 GW electricity-service requirement . OpenAI says the power is expected in phases from 2028 through 2032 . Georgia Power confirmed in August 2026 that the regulatory process cleared its large-load agreement, including up to 1,000 MW of flexible demand response that could be curtailed during high grid demand.

name: Servpac MTP Data Center
heading: 3. Servpac MTP Data Center — 1 MW Documented Available Power
brief: The Servpac MTP data center at 200 Kahelu Avenue in Mililani Technology Park occupies a 30,000-square-foot building designed for high-availability services. Its operator brochure reports 1 MW of available power , dual power distribution, backup generators, UPS equipment and redundant cooling. The facility earned Uptime Institute Tier IV Certification of Constructed Facility , reflecting its engineering focus on fault tolerance.

name: AlohaNAP, Kapolei
heading: 2. AlohaNAP, Kapolei — 2.7 MW Planned After Phase-One Expansion
brief: At 91-340 Farrington Highway in Kapolei , AlohaNAP provides a connection point for submarine-fiber routes, satellite traffic, regional carriers and cloud platforms. In October 2024, owners Harrison Street and 1547 Critical Systems Realty announced a 10,300-square-foot, 1.5 MW addition. Upon completion of the first phase, the complex was expected to have 22,800 square feet and 2.7 MW of total capacity . This is an announced development specification rather than confirmed energized computing capac

name: DRFortress, Honolulu
heading: 1. DRFortress, Honolulu — 4.2 MW of Backup Power
brief: DRFortress , at 3375 Koapaka Street in Honolulu , is described by its operator as Hawaii’s largest carrier-neutral commercial data center. The 65,000-square-foot facility supports approximately 800 colocation cabinets as well as cloud services, private suites, interconnection and disaster recovery. Its current owner, 1547 Critical Systems Realty , publishes a 4.2 MW backup power specification with N+1 redundancy. Backup generator capacity is not an IT-load rating or a measure of current utility

name: Meta Kuna Data Center
heading: 3. Meta Kuna Data Center — 198 MW Estimated Operating Campus Capacity
brief: Meta announced on September 3, 2026 that its Kuna Data Center is officially online . The site near Kuna-Mora and Cole roads represents an investment of more than $1.2 billion and involved about 1,600 construction workers at peak . Meta’s formal opening statement confirms operating status but does not disclose a verified facility or IT megawatt rating . The company continues building at the site, including two rapid-deployment buildings documented by BoiseDev in October .

name: Rhea Data Blacks Creek Campus
heading: 2. Rhea Data Blacks Creek Campus — 600 MW Preliminary Proposal
brief: The Rhea Data project, submitted by a subsidiary of Nevada-based Arevia Power, envisions a 600 MW data-processing complex south of Boise near Blacks Creek Reservoir and the Interstate 84 corridor . In September 2026, KIVI reported confirmation from the Bureau of Land Management of a roughly 4-million-square-foot , multi-building facility. The proposal involves about 3,700 acres of BLM-managed land across the broader project corridor and includes an on-site natural-gas power plant and electrical

name: Diode Ventures Gemstone Technology Park
heading: 1. Diode Ventures Gemstone Technology Park — 600–800 MW Full-Buildout Range
brief: Gemstone Technology Park is a 620-acre industrial data-center development at 3250 South Locust Grove Road near Barker Road in Kuna. A Diode Ventures representative told the April 2025 City Council hearing that the eventual campus might require 600–800 MW of electricity at full buildout , a range reported by the Idaho Statesman . The site is envisioned as a phased campus with several buildings, utility facilities and landscaped buffer areas. A reported investment above $1 billion is an anticipate

name: T5 Chicago IV, Grayslake
heading: 3. T5 Chicago IV, Grayslake — Approximately 1,550 MW Reported Grid Supply
brief: At Peterson and Alleghany roads in Grayslake, Lake County , T5 Data Centers’ Chicago IV is planned as a large phased hyperscale campus covering roughly 472–474 acres . The approved development envelope allows up to approximately 10 million square feet of floor area. Project reporting quotes 1.2 GW of potential IT load and roughly 1.55 GW of contracted ComEd electrical supply ; some sources round the secured service figure to 1.6 GW . The IT number describes capacity assigned to computing equipme

name: Project Cardinal, Yorkville
heading: 2. Project Cardinal, Yorkville — 1,800 MW Reported Planned Campus
brief: Project Cardinal , proposed by Pioneer Development, LLC , spans approximately 1,037 acres of farmland in Yorkville in Kendall County. The city’s application record describes 14 two-story data-center buildings totaling over 17 million square feet , two substations, a switchyard, seven stormwater basins and access roads. Independent project ledgers and contemporaneous filings report a planned 1.8 GW electrical scale; that is a development target rather than an amount approved for immediate deliver

name: Joliet Technology Center
heading: 1. Joliet Technology Center — 1,800 MW Developer Buildout Estimate
brief: Joliet Technology Center is a planned 795-acre campus southwest of Chicago, near South Rowell Road and Bernhard Road , developed by Hillwood and PowerHouse Data Centers. The developer advertises a possible $20 billion investment , a phased campus of approximately 24 buildings and 1.8 GW of proposed full-buildout electrical demand . The city’s March 2026 legislative record independently documents the 1,800 MW developer projection, making this tied first-place entry documented directly as a report

name: Project Beckham, Elkhart County
heading: 3. Project Beckham, Elkhart County — Approximately 1,500 MW Estimated, Tied
brief: Takanock’s Project Beckham is a proposed data-center development in Elkhart County near Goshen. In April 2025 testimony to Indiana utility regulators, Takanock founder Kenneth Davies described an estimated 1.5 GW data-center load and a dispute with Northern Indiana Public Service Company over the route and cost of electric service. Powered Lands’ project record summarizes the filing and identifies the proposal with Goshen.

name: Digital Realty, Kokomo
heading: 2. Digital Realty, Kokomo — Approximately 1,500 MW Proposed, Tied
brief: Digital Realty’s Kokomo proposal calls for three buildings on approximately 476 acres at Industrial Park North. The company describes about 1 GW of IT capacity across roughly 3 million square feet. In October reporting on the proposal , a Digital Realty representative was quoted as estimating that the fully built campus would need about 1.5 GW of total facility power . This is a reported estimate, not a finalized utility interconnection agreement. The two numbers measure different things: IT cap

name: Amazon Project Rainier, New Carlisle
heading: 1. Amazon Project Rainier, New Carlisle — Approximately 2,200 MW at Full Buildout
brief: Amazon Web Services’ New Carlisle campus in St. Joseph County is already partly operating and continues to expand. The published full-buildout figure is not a verified current utility draw. The South Bend Regional Chamber’s AWS environmental FAQ says the site is expected to use approximately 2.2 GW at completion . BitcoinVersus.Tech covered Amazon’s $11 billion Indiana announcement in 2024; the current campus is much further along than a land-only proposal.

name: COPT Defense, Van Meter
heading: 3. COPT Defense, Van Meter — Approximately 1,000 MW Estimated Capacity (Tied)
brief: COPT Defense Properties acquired a 365-acre parcel near Des Moines for $32 million in September 2024 to extend its data center shell-development business into Iowa. In its October 28, 2024 acquisition announcement , the company said the zoning could accommodate approximately 3.3 million square feet of future development with an estimated 1 GW of power capacity . That was a preliminary development figure, not a utility commitment to deliver 1 GW.

name: Tract Altoona Technology Park
heading: 2. Tract Altoona Technology Park — 1,000 MW Advertised Site Capacity (Tied)
brief: Tract’s official Altoona project page lists 1,000 MW of capacity for its technology park, describes the property as owned and in development , and states it covers 468 acres . Tract originally announced acquisition of 453 fully entitled acres in September 2025 , describing a 1 GW-plus opportunity on an existing 345 kV transmission corridor . The two published acreage numbers reflect different dated descriptions; the current project page’s 468-acre figure is used here instead of silently treating

name: QTS Cedar Rapids
heading: 1. QTS Cedar Rapids — Approximately 1,050–1,133 MW Reported Planned Scale
brief: QTS Data Centers’ August 8, 2025 announcement describes a seven-building campus on 612 acres at the Big Cedar Industrial Center in southwest Cedar Rapids. The Blackstone-backed company projected up to $10 billion of long-term investment . The developer and utility confirm that construction is occurring, unlike the mostly land-stage projects at Altoona and Van Meter. QTS does not disclose a single definitive full-campus MW rating in that announcement.

name: Red Wolf DCD Properties, Kansas City
heading: 3. Red Wolf DCD Properties, Kansas City — 600 MW Proposed
brief: The Red Wolf proposal would occupy land on both sides of Parallel Parkway near Kansas Speedway in western Wyandotte County. KCUR’s January 29, 2026 investigation , based on local utility and government proceedings, describes a roughly 548-acre development with a proposed 600 MW electrical requirement—approximately 300 MW north and 300 MW south of the parkway. The broader concept includes multiple data center buildings, major electrical substations and connecting infrastructure.

name: Project Bluestem, Tonganoxie
heading: 2. Project Bluestem, Tonganoxie — Up to 1,200 MW Proposed
brief: Project Bluestem , developed by Cloverleaf Infrastructure near the Tonganoxie Business Park in Leavenworth County, has expanded from an early 600 MW concept to an up-to-1.2 GW development scale reported during the September 16 county public meeting. The updated plan covers more than 1,000 acres near the Tonganoxie/Eudora I-70 interchange, according to KCTV’s contemporaneous reporting and local project tracking. This is a potential campus requirement, not independently tested IT power or a signed

name: Digital Realty, Astra Enterprise Park, De Soto
heading: 1. Digital Realty, Astra Enterprise Park, De Soto — 2,000 MW Eventual Utility Service
brief: Digital Realty’s June 22, 2026 investor announcement is the strongest capacity evidence in this Kansas ranking. The company said it acquired approximately 1,440 acres at Astra Enterprise Park , on the former Sunflower Army Ammunition Plant property in De Soto, in a transaction valued at approximately $475 million . It disclosed an Energy Service Agreement to provide 600 MW of utility power by early 2028 , rising to 2 GW at full delivery . The latter figure is a future contractual development obj

name: DOE Paducah AI Campus
heading: 3. DOE Paducah AI Campus — 1,800 MW Planned Utility Service
brief: The U.S. Department of Energy announced on July 29, 2026 that Brookfield , NextEra Energy , and three regional power organizations would pursue an AI and high-performance computing campus on land at the former Paducah Gaseous Diffusion Plant . The estimated private-sector program exceeds $100 billion , although that figure describes the proposed long-term infrastructure investment, not money already spent. The federal site retains transmission, water, roads, and other infrastructure from its ura

name: Rubix Data Centers, Russell
heading: 2. Rubix Data Centers, Russell — 2,000 MW Proposed Full Buildout
brief: At the former AK Steel works in Russell, Greenup County , Rubix Data Centers, a subsidiary of Spain-based Submer Group , proposes a phased AI campus on an industrial brownfield. The strongest primary evidence is the developer’s municipal due-diligence questionnaire submitted to the City of Russell . It describes approximately 500 acres , eight two-story buildings, and about 2 million square feet of total floor space. The company gives an initial phase near 155 MW , rising toward 2,000 MW of tota

name: Meta Mason County Campus
heading: 1. Meta Mason County Campus — 2,200 MW Reported Long-Term Scale
brief: Meta emerged publicly on October 13, 2026 as the company behind an enormous hyperscale data center proposal near Maysville in Mason County . The county’s Fiscal Court unanimously approved major project agreements involving Meta’s development affiliate, Crisham LLC , after officials had spent months negotiating under confidentiality arrangements. WVXU’s October 15 local reporting identifies a reported 2.2 GW long-term campus and roughly 2,900 acres of land. The 2.2 GW figure is reported developme

name: Applied Digital Delta Forge 1
heading: 3. Applied Digital Delta Forge 1 — 430 MW Planned Utility Power
brief: Applied Digital’s Delta Forge 1 is a purpose-built AI computing campus near Boyce in Rapides Parish . On January 22, 2026 , the developer said construction had started on two planned buildings designed to support an initial 430 MW of total utility power . It specified 300 MW of critical IT load within that initial design. This is a more concrete development commitment than an untethered site-capacity estimate, but not evidence that the full campus was electrically energized in 2026.

name: ONE Nuclear Project Barracuda
heading: 2. ONE Nuclear Project Barracuda — Up to 1,000 MW Proposed IT Capacity
brief: Project Barracuda entered Louisiana’s data center pipeline in September. In a September 10, 2026 company announcement that was also filed with the Securities and Exchange Commission , ONE Nuclear Energy described a proposed 1.2 GW Energy Park and Technology Campus , with up to approximately 1 GW of critical IT data center capacity . That is the ranking figure. It is a planning-level concept , not a signed tenant lease or commissioned server load.

name: Meta Hyperion, Richland Parish
heading: 1. Meta Hyperion, Richland Parish — 5,000 MW Planned Compute Capacity
brief: Meta Hyperion , near Holly Ridge in Richland Parish , is Louisiana’s largest documented AI campus. In its July 13, 2026 update , Meta announced an expansion of its ongoing Richland Parish project to five gigawatts of compute capacity . The expanded long-term investment exceeds $50 billion , and the site is intended to house Meta’s largest multi-gigawatt AI training cluster.
